chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban, from 'Anbasah, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام say: 'Ali عليه السلام did not consider there to be any wudu (ablution) due to madhy, nor washing of what of it touched the garment, except in the case of the greater fluid.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment that may be affected by the fluid
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the greater fluid, meaning the discharge treated with a more significant purity ruling
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.غَسْلَ: washing or cleansing in relation to impurity on clothing
key_terms.وُضُوءًا: ritual ablution required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) or washing from clothes in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling regarding madhy, stating that it does not necessitate wudu (ablution) nor washing it from clothing. An exception is mentioned for the greater fluid, indicating a distinction in rulings between lesser and greater bodily discharges in matters of taharah.
